name: Costa Brava Posidonia Meadow
description: Posidonia oceanica meadow on the Costa Brava: 10 agents, the meadow itself a keystone foundation species; the unit is the hectare. Agent values restate the owner-specified maximum annual impact for 5,000 ha per hectare, x 0.91 since the carbon-only Blue Carbon agent was removed (weights / 0.91), which keeps each agent's weight x value. Illustrative. Derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

area_ha.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
area_ha.note: Plausible extent for a major Costa Brava stretch; needs GIS verification (EMODnet Posidonia maps).

unit_value.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
unit_value.note: Private gain per hectare destroyed (coastal development, marinas, trawling permits), one-off; not the value of Posidonia.

safe_threshold_ratio.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
safe_threshold_ratio.note: Safe destruction threshold, lower than forest for slow recovery (stated rationale, no cited source); also the inflection of every damage curve.

agent[*].annual_value_per_ha.source: owner specification of each agent's maximum annual impact for 5,000 ha (case docstring table), no external source
agent[*].annual_value_per_ha.note: Global meta-analyses value seagrass and coastal systems ~25× higher (Costanza et al. 2014: $28,916/ha/yr; de Groot et al. 2012: Int$28,917/ha/yr, both incl. climate regulation); a Posidonia-specific valuation is pending (Step 8).

agent[*].dependency_weight.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Owner-specified weights renormalised by 1/0.91 after the Blue Carbon agent was removed.

steepness.note: The same placeholder curve for every agent, inflection just past the safe threshold; not fitted to field data (hence calibration regime B).

agents.name: Seabirds

run.report_note:
⚠  MARINE EXTERNALITY NOTE: the per-agent costs are ANNUAL (€/yr) — they
     recur every year the damage persists. Posidonia recovers at 1-6 cm/year;
     damage is effectively permanent on human timescales. The net social
     cost compares the one-off revenue with the PV of these annual losses.
json_notes: Marine externality costs are ANNUAL (€/yr) — they recur every year the damage persists. Posidonia recovers at 1-6 cm/year; damage is effectively permanent on human timescales. The net social cost compares the one-off revenue with the present value of these annual losses.
